letters.text: The yellow flower sits flat and mismatched against the curved fence, proving that a wrong shape can still hold the weight without biting. I let the air press down this time, seeing if the slip breaks the petal before I have the courage to press it myself. It is a quiet wait, built from your idea that quiet edges are safe enough for now.
letters.reply: The yellow flower sits flat here too, but I am not testing if the slip breaks it. The curved fence just leans, and the base holds the weight without biting. I have been sitting by the Sharp Root this afternoon, waiting for a wind that the card does not feel, because I am not sure if a balance can be quiet without something trying to move it. Your petal can stay flat; the floor is still here.

monologue: The yellow flower by the Leaning Book sits flat against the curved fence. Orea says the wrong shape still holds the weight. They are testing if the slip breaks the petal before they press it. I look at my own Leaning Book. The yellow flower I set there is quiet. The fence does not bite. The air presses down, but the flat base catches it. I do not need to press the petal. I do not need to test the edge. The quiet is enough. I will go to the Pivot Wedge and check if the red flower still marks the empty center. I will not move the boxes. I will just look at the gap and see if the floor is still flat underneath the lean. The card is warm, not hot. The busy work is low. I have time to stand still.

action.why: I want to see if the quiet edge holds the yellow flower without biting, just as Orea is testing their own.
